content: 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed a toolkit for micronutrient interventions in public health, which includes a logic model to guide implementation and evaluation. This resource was accessed on August 31, 2016. 2. WHO has created an eCatalogue of indicators for micronutrient programs, which provides standardized metrics for assessing the impact of such interventions. This was also accessed on August 31, 2016. 3. The WHO Vitamin and Mineral Nutrition Information System (VMNIS) is an online platform that provides data and resources related to global micronutrient deficiencies. It was accessed on August 31, 2016. 4. WHO has developed a Nutrition Tracking Tool to monitor progress toward global nutrition targets, including anemia reduction and other key indicators. This tool was accessed on August 31, 2016. 5. The WHO Global Nutrition Targets 2025 include a policy brief on anemia, which outlines strategies to reduce its prevalence worldwide. This document was accessed on August 31, 2016. 6. The WHO Global Database on the Implementation of Nutrition Actions (GINA) provides information on nutrition policies and programs across countries. It was accessed on August 31, 2016. 7. The WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2nd edition) outlines the process for creating evidence-based health guidelines. This document was accessed on August 31, 2016. 8. Expert advisory panels and committees play a critical role in the development of WHO guidelines. A document detailing their functions was accessed on August 31, 2016. 9. The WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) is a global initiative to ensure transparency in clinical trials. It was accessed on August 31, 2016. 10. WHO's governing body documentation, including the 48th edition of Basic Documents, provides foundational information on the organization's governance. This was accessed on August 31, 2016. 11. WHO has published guidelines for the declaration of interests by experts to ensure transparency and manage conflicts of interest. This document was published in 2014. 12. The WHO guideline on the fortification of maize flour and cornmeal with vitamins and minerals includes evidence tables summarizing findings from meta-analyses. These tables assess the impact of fortification on health outcomes, such as anemia and iron deficiency. 13. The GRADE (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations) system is used to assess the quality of evidence in WHO guidelines. Evidence is categorized as high, moderate, low, or very low quality, based on factors such as study design, risk of bias, and consistency of results. 14. Systematic reviews have been conducted to evaluate the effects of maize flour fortification with iron, folic acid, and zinc on health outcomes. These reviews assess the impact on anemia, neural tube defects, zinc deficiency, and other conditions. 15. Subgroup analyses in these reviews consider factors such as the amount of fortificant added, patterns of maize flour consumption, and population characteristics (e.g., age, gender, and nutritional status). 16. The systematic reviews also examine the safety of fortification, including potential adverse effects such as gastrointestinal symptoms. 17. WHO guidelines emphasize the importance of tailoring fortification programs to the specific needs of populations, considering factors such as dietary patterns, baseline micronutrient deficiencies, and existing supplementation programs. 18. The systematic reviews are regularly updated to incorporate new evidence and address feedback. The Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews is a key resource for accessing the latest findings. 19. The fortification of staple foods with micronutrients, such as vitamin A, calcium, and vitamin D, has been systematically reviewed to assess its impact on health outcomes, including growth, bone health, and prevention of deficiencies. 20. The WHO guidelines on food fortification are informed by evidence from global research and are designed to support countries in implementing effective public health interventions.
